stage: KV cache write replacement: implemented and firing; NOT numerically correct
what_it_replaces: the two IndexPutOps that write projected K and V into the cache. The operator inventory said this one would need an out-parameter form, and it does: the kernel writes through its Cache argument and the graph's cache is a function argument, which one-shot bufferize treats as writable.

structure.shared_position: the mask kernel and the cache write both need one absolute slot per token, so they share a single i32 [S] buffer rather than carrying two
structure.new_cases_built: layout_context_8x16x128 and layout_context_8x1x128, added to tools/generate_elementwise.py and built through the full Triton -> triton-riscv -> MLIR -> Buddy lowering -> NR chain
structure.result: 4 replacements (2 caches x 2 graphs), uncovered still 0, 22 external calls per graph

numeric_result.reading: the transpose made it worse, which means either the layout claim is backwards or something else is wrong and the transpose merely changed how it is wrong

reasoning_about_the_layout.graph: index_put(dest=[1,8,512,128], index=[16] along dim 2, value=[1,8,16,128]) means value is [batch, heads, sequence, head_dim]
reasoning_about_the_layout.kernel: kv_cache_update_position indexes `X + (token*8 + head)*128 + channel`, i.e. [sequence, heads, head_dim]
reasoning_about_the_layout.so: a dim-1/dim-2 swap is needed -- which is what layout_context does, and what I added. Since it made things worse, this reasoning needs checking against a standalone kernel test rather than more of the same argument.

next_diagnostic.what: check whether the attention reads the same buffer the cache-write call writes. The graph's IndexPut produced a NEW tensor that its consumers read; my rewrite makes them read the cache INPUT instead, and if one-shot bufferize decided the attention needs a copy of that input, it sees the pre-write cache.
next_diagnostic.how: dump the lowered LLVM IR and follow the pointer the cache-write call receives into the descriptor the attention call receives; if they differ the aliasing is broken
next_diagnostic.alternative_fix: write into a caller-owned workspace buffer that is initialised from the cache once per call, so the write and the read share a buffer the graph never treats as read-only -- but that must preserve the cache across decode steps, so it has to be the same buffer every call

bug_found_along_the_way: the first version named a loop variable `index`, shadowing the case-table parameter; every lookup raised AttributeError on an AddOp

board.note: host-only work; the full-model run was not disturbed

standalone_kernel_test.what: called _mlir_ciface_kernel_kv_cache_update_position_16x8x128_cap512 directly on the host with X[s,h,0] = s*1000 + h*10 + 7 and Position = arange(16)
standalone_kernel_test.conclusion: the kernel reads X as [sequence, heads, head_dim] and writes Cache[head, slot, dim] exactly as the source says. My layout reasoning was RIGHT and the transpose is required.
standalone_kernel_test.so: the numeric failure is NOT a layout problem. With the transpose correct and the result still wrong -- and worse than without it -- the remaining suspect is the graph's dataflow: the attention may be reading a buffer the write never reached.

isolated_by_comparing_the_written_cache.method: both host runs save the cache the graph returns (prefill_kv_key/value), so the write can be judged on its own rather than through the logits
isolated_by_comparing_the_written_cache.good_run_attention_only: non-zero slots per head: 0..17 -- the graph's IndexPut writes the whole prompt
isolated_by_comparing_the_written_cache.reading: slots 1..15 are ZERO in the replaced run. That is the signature of a Position array that is all zeros: every token is told to write slot 0, so each one overwrites the last and only slot 0 survives.
isolated_by_comparing_the_written_cache.so_the_defect_is: the position buffer the cache-write kernel receives, not the kernel, not the layout, and not the transpose
isolated_by_comparing_the_written_cache.puzzle: the SAME buffer feeds the attention mask, and in the attention-only run that works -- the mask clearly uses 0..15, since the logits match FP32 to 1e-7. So the buffer is filled correctly there. Something about the KV path either receives a different buffer or zeroes it.
candidates: the attention rewrite and the KV rewrite may not be sharing the node I think: the report shows both keyed to attn__scaled_dot_product_flash_attention_for_cpu_position, so a name check passes -- but the host runner fills by NAME across a workspace list that contains two entries with that name, one [16] for prefill and one [1] for decode, and an index/dtype mix-up between them would produce exactly this
the descriptor the kernel receives may point at a different buffer than the one the host fills
isolated_by_comparing_the_written_cache.next_step: print the position buffer immediately before the call in the host runner, so the value the kernel is handed is observed rather than inferred

root_cause.symptom: the cache came back with slots {0, 16, 17} only, and adding the K/V transpose made the logits worse rather than better
root_cause.cause: a SYMBOL NAME COLLISION. call_types is shared across graphs and keyed by the wrapper symbol. I named the layout wrapper `kv_<node>_layout`, without the case name -- and the prefill and decode graphs both have a node called index_put, so the decode graph's entry overwrote the prefill's. One wrapper then served both, calling the DECODE layout kernel layout_context_8x1x128 for the prefill, i.e. transposing only the first token and leaving the rest of the K/V block unconverted.
root_cause.fix: the symbol now carries the case: kv_<node>_<case>, giving kv_index_put_layout_context_8x16x128 and ..._8x1x128 as separate wrappers
root_cause.how_it_was_found: reading the generated adapters, where the wrapper for the prefill layout call visibly invoked the 8x1 kernel

what_made_it_hard: the report and the adapter used different names for the same thing, so a grep for the case name in the adapters returned nothing and looked like the case was missing rather than mis-wired
the transposed run being WORSE than the untransposed one was the clue: a transpose applied to one token out of sixteen is worse than none
